run_277_runtime.ego_shutdown: SIGINT teardown produced invalid-context RCLError; exit -6

code_change.behavior: Retain the exact adapter clock/source-stamp comparison when a future sample is detected and emit one epoch-scoped JSON error line; health thresholds and lock behavior are unchanged.

verified_findings: In #274 and #275, the adapter remained valid TRACKING and did not reproduce propagated_from_future. #275 external probe clock estimates had scheduling-sensitive outliers and cannot establish the adapter clock for a raw DDS message.
In instrumented full-stack static run #277, all 665 received adapter status samples were valid TRACKING. The exact internal future-observation log remained absent because the guard did not trigger.
The #277 external raw propagated stream had source-age-at-probe-receipt from -2 to +3 ms, with no sample below -20 ms; max observer receipt gap was 332.819 ms, so these remain probe-side values.
The earlier #273 propagated_from_future lock remains a single observation without captured internal source/clock pair. #274, #275 and #277 do not establish its cause or disprove it.
The #276 harness attempt did not execute build or simulation and is excluded.
limitations: All executed comparison runs used static D435i, with no truth, PX4, controller, or goal. They do not test motion, map coverage, planning, navigation, or flight.
The #277 full-stack EGO stayed INIT, logged repeated no odom, and exited with invalid-context RCLError during SIGINT teardown; this run does not qualify EGO handoff or clean shutdown.
The diagnostic repeat is exploratory and does not change the 20 ms future tolerance or any acceptance threshold; GOAL B/P2 acceptance is not inferred.
The static EGO launches in #275 and #277 used odometry_topic:=odom, not /localization/optimized_imu_odom; their timeout/INIT observations do not assess EGO with the correct input wiring.
